name: 599. A provider added at runtime answers to its prefix on its first request (prefix-on-add)
description:
TXE-7501 / PR #339. A custom provider added through POST /api/providers is built by core on its first request, and its name became a known model prefix only then. So the first request naming it, "<provider>/model", parsed to no provider: the model catalog sent it to whichever provider claimed the model string, or refused it, and the new provider was reached at best as a fallback.

Each row creates its own run-scoped OpenAI-backed provider with its key in the same POST (adding the key later through /keys builds the provider first and hides the bug), then sends the very first request on it. The row pins that the new provider served it, that the prefix was stripped before routing, and that the upstream received the bare model. Row 1 is /v1/chat/completions, row 2 /v1/responses. Each row deletes its provider; providers an aborted run left behind are swept after ten minutes.
